correctness.rationale: For all \(A>B>0\) and \(K,k,\tau>0\), integration of the exact two-impulse trajectories gives positive rational R_{AB}, R_{BA}. The exact numerator factor Ky(A-B)(1-y)(zD-ABy^2) over a positive denominator implies one and only one crossing. D-ABy=(K+A+B)(K+y(A+B))+AB(1-y)^2>0 forces its z-root to lie in (0,y), equivalent to a unique T>tau. Separate post-second-pulse difference (A-B)(y-1)e^{-k(t-tau)} is negative at all t>tau. The executable checker independently verifies exact identities, three rational horizon cases and 768 numerical integrals; universal proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: The 2023 full public paper solves a Richards PDE irrigation control problem and uses a Feddes-type uptake, not this scalar exact two-impulse integrated saturating-score comparison. The earlier 2016 full open article uses a first-order water balance with a state constraint and control optimality conditions, not this fixed-two-pulse-horizon phase law. Indexed comparable published records treat runoff thresholds, stream depletion and static nutrient ordering under non-equivalent dynamics/objectives; no reviewed source was established to imply the formula. This is only a best-knowledge result, with older nonlinear dosing/scheduling work a residual risk.
residual_risks: An older paper on unequal bolus dosing with saturating cumulative output could give an equivalent formula without irrigation terminology.
Semantic record summaries for other research items do not constitute full-document noncoverage findings.
Phenomenological Monod score and constant exponential drainage are assumptions, not empirical calibration or a statement about Richards/Feddes dynamics.

value.rationale: The exact universal one-horizon inversion is a sharp structural decision boundary for allocating a fixed two-pulse moisture budget: initially large-first is optimal, ultimately small-first is optimal, despite post-second-pulse instantaneous score always favoring small-first. The threshold is analytically explicit for arbitrary positive dose, interval, decay and saturation parameters, and hence gives a reproducible counterexample to horizon-independent order rankings, not an arbitrary isolated computation. The result is a theoretical calibration benchmark, not an operational irrigation recommendation.
